description: Kurumba painting, or Kurumbar painting, is a prehistoric art form utilizing painting that depict aspects of tribal Kurumba life in the Nilgiri Mountains, located in modern-day Tamil Nadu, India. The earliest documented reference to the continuity of Kurumba paintings on dwelling structures in the Nilgiris dates to 1871–1872, reported by James Wilkinson Breeks in 1873. These visual representations are historically linked to prehistoric and Neolithic rock art, estimated to be over 3,000 years old, discovered at the Jackanarai and Eluthu Paarai archaeological sites in the Nilgiri Hills of Tamil Nadu in 1984.
